items.definition:
a person who tries hard or makes an effort
She's a real trier, always giving her best.

The design of a set of characters.
Choose a clear typeface for your presentation.

A tower from which to keep watch.
The guard stood in the watchtower, scanning the horizon.

an open-air venue used for entertainment
The concert was held in the ancient amphitheatre.

active hostility or opposition
There was clear antagonism between the two rival teams.

a person who offers an argument in defense of something controversial
He became an apologist for the government's controversial policies.

fuel derived directly from living matter
Many cars can now run on biofuel, reducing carbon emissions.

a long, thick elastic cord, typically with a hook at each end
He secured the luggage with a bungee cord.

a dramatic and exciting ending to an episode of a series, leaving the audience in suspense
The season finale ended on a shocking cliffhanger.

an ordinary person, without noble rank or title
In medieval times, commoners had few rights compared to the nobility.

reduction
The company announced significant cutbacks in spending.

device for exchanging
The heat exchanger transfers thermal energy between fluids.

any substance that is used as food
The store sells a variety of foodstuffs, including fresh produce and canned goods.

a dye prepared from the plant Lawsonia inermis, used to color hair and skin
She got a beautiful henna tattoo on her hand.

a siren or horn, especially on a vehicle
The train blew its hooter as it approached the crossing.

The rise and fall of the voice in speaking.
Her intonation clearly showed her surprise.

A toy consisting of a tube containing mirrors and pieces of colored glass or paper, whose reflections produce changing patterns.
The child looked through the kaleidoscope and gasped at the patterns.

A person who steals goods, typically during a war or riot.
The police arrested several looters after the protest.

A lake or sea inlet, especially in Ireland.
We went fishing in the lough.

A person who writes the lyrics for songs.
The lyricist collaborated with the composer on the new musical.

The guidance provided by a mentor.
She benefited greatly from her mentorship with an experienced colleague.

a place where a boat or ship is moored
The boat broke free from its mooring during the storm.

the sport or activity of climbing mountains
Mountaineering requires specialized equipment and extensive training.

the contradiction or denial of something
The word "not" is used to form a negation in English sentences.

the state of being unified or whole
The spiritual leader spoke about the oneness of all living things.

the quality of being opaque; the degree to which something is opaque
The opacity of the glass made it impossible to see through.

a deficit in a bank account caused by drawing more money than the account holds
He incurred an overdraft fee because he spent more than he had in his account.

the origin or descent of a person
His parentage was a mystery, as he was adopted at a young age.

the Christian festival celebrating the descent of the Holy Spirit on the apostles
Many churches celebrate Pentecost with special services and events.

physiotherapist
I have an appointment with the physio next week for my knee.

advocate of protectionism
The new trade policy was criticized by free-market advocates as being protectionist.

an open-top two-seater car
He drove his vintage roadster along the coastal highway.

a quick cut with scissors; a small piece cut off
She gave the loose thread a quick snip with her scissors.

a sudden gush or burst
There was a sudden spurt of water from the broken pipe.

a thin sheet of material with a design cut out of it
She used a stencil to paint the letters on the sign.

a person who tends the furnace of a steam engine or boiler
The stoker shoveled coal into the train's engine.

a hard, durable timber from a tropical tree, used for furniture and shipbuilding
The outdoor furniture was made of solid teak.

a child between the ages of 8 and 12, considered too old for toys but too young for teenage interests
The store has a section specifically for tween fashion.

a generator that produces alternating current
The mechanic said the car's alternator needed to be replaced.

an area of barren land with eroded ridges and peaks
The explorers ventured into the desolate badlands.

a style of jazz developed in the 1940s
Bebop is known for its fast tempos and complex harmonies.

a large bird of prey, typically a vulture or a hawk
A buzzard circled high above the fields, looking for prey.

a small breed of dog with short legs and a fox-like head
The Queen of England was famous for her love of corgis.

a gradual increase in loudness or intensity
The music built to a dramatic crescendo.

a curse word; an annoying or unpleasant person or thing
He let out a loud cuss when he hit his thumb with the hammer.

a claim to something; a right to something
I call dibs on the front seat!

a small boat, especially an inflatable rubber boat
They rowed the small dinghy out to the yacht.

a ladle; a bird that dives for food; part of a constellation
He used a dipper to scoop water from the well.

a person who travels from place to place without a home or job
He lived like a drifter, never staying in one town for long.

something that improves or increases the quality of something
This new software is a great enhancer for productivity.

a person who asks for information
The enquirer waited patiently for a response.

artworks created by fans of a work of fiction
She spends hours creating fanart of her favorite anime characters.

a person who plays the fiddle (violin)
The old fiddler played a lively tune.

a unit of distance, equal to 220 yards (about 201 meters)
The horse won the race by three furlongs.

talk, chatter (informal)
She loves to have a good gab with her friends.

a material used to fill gaps between tiles
We need to clean the grout between the bathroom tiles.

a group of chemical elements or a type of lamp
The car's headlights use halogen bulbs.

a barbed spear used for hunting large fish or whales
The whaler threw the harpoon with great force.

hazardous materials (abbreviation)
The hazmat team was called to deal with the chemical spill.

a long-legged wading bird
We saw a flock of ibises near the riverbank.

a person who is guided by ideals rather than practical considerations
He's an idealist who believes in the power of positive change.

a mutual connection between two or more things
There is a strong interconnection between climate change and human activity.

a slight irregular movement, especially in an electrical signal or a person's body
The video signal had a slight jitter.

a long, single-edged sword used by Japanese samurai
He displayed an antique katana on the wall.
